title: Kidnapped to Be Sold on the Dark Web. Then No One Believed Her.
titles: Kidnapped to Be Sold on the Dark Web. No One Believed Her.
She Was Told She'd Be Auctioned on the Dark Web
Why Didn't She Run? The Chloe Ayling Kidnapping
description: In July 2017, a 20-year-old British model flew to Milan for a photoshoot and was kidnapped, drugged and told she would be auctioned on the dark web by a gang called the Black Death Group. This is the true story of Chloe Ayling: the fake job, the six days in a farmhouse near Turin, the man behind the mask, and why so many people refused to believe her.
sources: Milan court verdict, 11 June 2018 (AP / CBS News)
BBC: Chloe Ayling: My Unbelievable Kidnapping (2025)

scenes.say: In July 2017, a twenty year old model from London flew to Milan for a photoshoot. A few hours later, she woke up in the boot of a car, inside a bag, with her wrists cuffed.

visuals.ai: the grand hall of Milan's central station
an empty photo studio with lights
the open boot of a car at night

scenes.say: The men who took her said she would be sold. Not on a street corner. On the dark web, to the highest bidder.

visuals.ai: a laptop glowing in a dark room
rows of servers in blue light

scenes.say: Her name was Chloe Ayling. And the strangest part of her story isn't what happened in those six days. It's what happened after, when she came home, and almost nobody believed her.
To understand how it happened, we have to start with a simple email. A job offer that looked completely normal.

visuals.ai: an email inbox on a laptop
a hand holding a phone with a new message

scenes.say: Chloe was from Coulsdon, in south London. She had a young son, and she was trying to build a modelling career. Her agent was a man named Phil Green, who ran a small agency and booked jobs for her.

visuals.ai: a suburban high street in south London
a fashion shoot behind the scenes

scenes.say: Earlier that year, a photographer had tried to book her for a shoot in Paris. It was cancelled. Then, in July, the same kind of request came back, this time for Milan. The photographer called himself Andre Lazio.

visuals.ai: a professional camera on a table

scenes.say: It looked like a real job. A flight, a studio, a fee. Thousands of young models take trips exactly like this every year. Chloe packed a bag and flew to Italy.

visuals.ai: the view from a plane window

scenes.say: Fake jobs are one of the oldest tricks there are. A stranger with a camera, a great offer, a trip abroad. Usually the trap is money. This time, the trap was the person herself.

visuals.ai: a passport and a boarding pass

scenes.say: The address she was given was not a studio. It was a quiet building on the edge of the city. When she walked in, two men in ski masks grabbed her from behind.
One held her down. The other pushed a needle into her arm. It was ketamine, a strong sedative. Within minutes, she was unconscious.
According to the prosecutors, she was handcuffed, zipped inside a large canvas bag, and loaded into the boot of a car. Then the car drove west, out of Milan, toward the mountains.
When she woke up, she was in a farmhouse in a tiny village called Viù, in the hills near Turin. For the first night, she was cuffed to a piece of furniture.

visuals.ai: a small mountain village in Piedmont
an old stone farmhouse in the hills
an old wooden chest of drawers

scenes.say: And then one of her captors, a man who spoke English, started explaining the rules.

visuals.ai: the dark mountain valleys above Turin

scenes.say: He told her he worked for a criminal organisation called the Black Death Group. A gang, he said, that kidnapped women and sold them in secret auctions on the dark web.

visuals.ai: lines of code on a dark screen
a silhouette in front of a monitor

scenes.say: The dark web is a part of the internet you can't reach with a normal browser. Sites there use special software that hides who runs them and who visits them. It's where stolen data, drugs and weapons are sold. And it's the perfect place to build a legend.

The software that makes this possible is called Tor. It actually began as research by the United States Navy, to protect secret communications. Today anyone can download it. Most people who use it just want privacy. But it also hides criminals.

visuals.ai: an onion cut in half, showing its layers

scenes.say: Some dark web markets were very real. In 2013 the FBI shut down Silk Road, a site that sold drugs to over a hundred thousand buyers. So when someone said women were being auctioned on the dark web, it didn't sound impossible. That's exactly why the threat worked.

search: FBI headquarters J. Edgar Hoover Building

scenes.say: A group with that name had been talked about online for years. Interpol had looked into it in 2015. But the photos of 'victims' on its sites were later believed to be fake. Nobody could prove it was anything more than a scary story.
Back in London, on the morning after Chloe disappeared, her agent received an email from someone who signed only with two letters: M D.
The message demanded three hundred thousand euros. If the money wasn't paid, it said, Chloe would be auctioned on the dark web on the sixteenth of July.
Her agent went straight to the British consulate in Milan. Italian police searched the address of the fake studio. They found some of her clothes. But Chloe was gone.

visuals.ai: an Italian police car in Milan

scenes.say: The deadline came closer. Three hundred thousand euros is a fortune for a small modelling agency. Nobody paid. And with every hour, the sixteenth of July got nearer.

visuals.ai: an old clock face close up

scenes.say: Inside the farmhouse, the man who held her told her a strange story. He said he was part of the gang, but that he was on her side. He said he was trying to protect her from the others.

visuals.ai: a dim room with a small window

scenes.say: He showed her photos of other women he claimed had already been sold. He told her the gang was watching, and that if she ran, they would find her.

visuals.ai: a pile of photographs on a table
a security camera on a wall

scenes.say: Chloe had to make a choice. Fight, and risk everything. Or play along. She chose to play along. She was calm, she was polite, she let him believe she trusted him. Later, she said it was the only way she could see to stay alive.

visuals.ai: a single candle in the dark

scenes.say: And then came the part of the story that the world would never stop talking about. During those six days, he took her into a town to buy shoes. She was in public. People were around. And she didn't run.

Why? She later said she was terrified. She believed the gang was real, and that someone was watching her every move. Running in a shop felt more dangerous than staying with the man who said he would protect her.
Then, according to her account, he told her something that changed everything. The gang had a rule. They didn't sell mothers. And Chloe had a two year old son at home.
On Monday the seventeenth of July, six days after she vanished, Chloe walked into the British consulate in Milan. And the man walking next to her was her kidnapper.

visuals.ai: a Milan street in the morning
a British flag on a building

scenes.say: He seemed to think he was the hero of the story. He had 'rescued' her from the gang. Police arrested him on the spot.
Cameras around the city had caught the two of them together, and the investigators quickly understood something. There was no big gang. There was this man, his brother, and a plan.

visuals.ai: a street camera on a pole

scenes.say: No ransom was ever paid. The man who had spent thousands of euros on the plan walked away with nothing at all. Except handcuffs of his own.

visuals.ai: a few euro coins on a table

scenes.say: His name was Lukasz Herba. He was thirty years old, from Poland, and he lived in Oldbury, a quiet town in the West Midlands of England. He worked with computers.

visuals.ai: a quiet town in the English Midlands

scenes.say: Andre Lazio, the photographer, was him. M D, the man who wrote the ransom email, was also him. And the Black Death Group, the investigators decided, was a story he had made up.

Prosecutors said he had spent at least ten thousand euros on the plan. He bought the ski masks. And afterwards, he asked his brother Michal to clean the boot of the car, so that no hair would be left behind.

And then came a detail almost nobody expected. Chloe and Lukasz were not complete strangers. According to evidence heard in court, they had been in contact on Facebook, and had met in person at least once, before her son was born.

visuals.ai: a social network page on a laptop

scenes.say: It didn't work. Investigators later linked Michal to the crime too.

In court, Lukasz told a different story every time. He said he loved Chloe. He said she had agreed to the whole thing, to make herself famous. He said he wanted to help her with money. He even said the plan was inspired by a film.

visuals.ai: the Palace of Justice in Milan

scenes.say: And that last claim, that Chloe had been in on it, was the one the newspapers loved most.
When Chloe came home, she expected sympathy. Instead, she got suspicion. The British press asked one question again and again. If she was really kidnapped, why didn't she run in the shoe shop?
People studied her face in interviews. She wasn't crying. She was calm, sometimes she smiled. On live television, she was questioned so hard that many viewers thought she was the one on trial.

lines: So they called her a liar.

scenes.say: Online, strangers called her a liar. Some said it was a publicity stunt. Some said she had planned it with him. The man who kidnapped her had told the same story, and millions of people repeated it for him.

It didn't help that, a few months later, she appeared on a celebrity reality show. To her critics, that was proof she was chasing fame. To her, it was a chance to tell her side, in front of millions of people who had already made up their minds.

Years later, Chloe would learn something about herself that explained a lot. In 2025, a documentary showed her receiving a diagnosis of autism. She had never reacted to fear the way people expected her to. That was never proof she was lying.
But in court, the evidence spoke louder than the headlines. On the eleventh of June, 2018, a court in Milan found Lukasz Herba guilty of kidnapping for ransom.
The prosecutor had asked for sixteen years and eight months. The judges gave him more. Sixteen years and nine months. They said Chloe could have died.

His lawyer argued that because Chloe came home unhurt, the sentence should have been no more than eight years. The court didn't agree. Chloe's own lawyer said he would ask for half a million euros in damages, but admitted Herba would probably never be able to pay.

visuals.label: Damages her lawyer wanted
visuals.note: Separate civil case; Herba was unlikely to pay

scenes.say: The next year, his brother Michal was convicted too, after being sent from Britain to stand trial in Italy.
But this isn't a story with a clean ending. On appeal, both sentences were cut. Lukasz's was reduced to about twelve years. Michal's was cut to less than six, and he was released early.
By 2024, reports said Lukasz Herba could be a free man within months. Neither brother is allowed back into the United Kingdom.

visuals.ai: a prison fence with barbed wire

scenes.say: Chloe didn't disappear. She wrote a book about what happened to her, called Kidnapped. And in 2024, the BBC turned her story into a drama, made with her help.
In 2025 came a documentary, in her own words. She said she wanted the facts laid out at last, and she asked people to stop judging victims by the way they act.
She has said that what hurt most was never the six days. It was the years of being told, by strangers, that she had made it all up.

visuals.ai: a silhouette looking out of a window

scenes.say: So what does this story really teach us? First. Check every job offer that seems too good. A photographer you've never met, a free trip abroad, a studio address nobody can confirm. Those are the warning signs.
Second. The most powerful weapon in this crime wasn't a needle or handcuffs. It was a story. The Black Death Group didn't need to exist. It only needed her to believe it did.

visuals.ai: a man's shadow on a wall

scenes.say: And third. Never judge a victim by how she reacts. Some people scream. Some people freeze. Some people smile, stay calm and play along, because that's how they survive.

Because in the end, the Black Death Group never auctioned anyone. A man with a laptop invented a monster, and for six days, a young mother had to live inside his lie. Then, for years, the rest of the world made her live inside it again.

visuals.ai: a lone laptop on a table

scenes.say: If you like dark true stories about crime, money and power, subscribe to Midnight Archive. There's always another file in the archive.
